name: spin-windup
concept: A rotation that starts slowly and accelerates through each turn, like a motor winding up to speed. Use it when a process is gathering momentum rather than already at full speed.

name: spin-surge
concept: A rotation that speeds up through the middle of each turn and eases at the ends. It reads as effortful, mechanical work rather than a flat, constant spin.

name: spin-flywheel
concept: A rotation that starts fast and decelerates across the turn, like a flywheel coasting down before the next push. Suits a process driven by bursts of effort.

name: spin-anticipate
concept: A small backward dip before the rotation launches forward, like a pitcher winding up before the throw. Gives a spinner a sense of readying itself.

name: spin-overshoot
concept: A rotation that swings slightly past a full turn before easing back into place. Gives a spinner a springy, elastic finish each cycle.

name: spin-crank
concept: A rotation with visibly increasing angular speed within each turn, like a hand crank being pulled through its arc. Suggests manual, ratcheted effort.

name: spin-breathe
concept: A rotation with a single gentle scale pulse per turn, as if the spinner is breathing while it works. Softer and calmer than a plain spin.

name: spin-inhale
concept: A rotation where the element grows early in the turn and settles back by the end, like a single deep inhale carried through the motion. Distinct from an even, centered pulse.

name: spin-pulse-double
concept: A rotation with two small scale pulses per turn, once on each half. Reads as a steady, ticking heartbeat layered onto ordinary spinning.

name: orbit-breathe
concept: A slow rotation combined with a wide scale swell and a small sideways drift, as if the spinner breathes while circling a point. Calmer and larger than a simple pulse.

name: spin-throb
concept: A sharp single scale kick near the start of each turn, followed by a plain smooth rotation for the rest of the cycle. Reads as a quick heartbeat kick, not a continuous pulse.

name: spin-billow
concept: A slow rotation with two wide, gentle scale swells offset from the turn's start, like a sail billowing in a light wind. Softer and slower than a double pulse.

name: spin-tick
concept: A rotation that jumps in four quarter-turn steps with a clear pause between each, like a clock's second hand ticking. Stepped, not smooth.

name: spin-ratchet
concept: A rotation that advances in six short steps with a brief hold between each, like a ratchet wrench catching its teeth. Quicker and busier than spin-tick.

name: spin-notch
concept: A quick rotation that snaps through eight small notches with short pauses between each. Feels crisp and mechanical, like a dial clicking past marked positions.

name: spin-index
concept: A slow rotation that advances in three long steps with generous pauses, like an indexing table turning between fixed positions. Deliberate rather than busy.

name: spin-cog
concept: A stepped rotation where each quarter-turn slightly overshoots and settles, like a gear tooth catching and rocking into place. More mechanical than a clean step.

name: spin-stepper
concept: A rotation broken into twelve fine, even micro-steps, like a stepper motor driving a dial. Reads as precise and mechanical rather than smooth.

name: orbit-wobble
concept: A rotation combined with a small circular drift, as if the spinner traces a tiny orbit while it turns. More alive than a rotation fixed to one point.

name: orbit-drift
concept: A rotation on a wider circular path that also swells and shrinks slightly as it drifts away from and back toward center. More pronounced than orbit-wobble.

name: spin-teeter
concept: A rotation with a small side-to-side sway layered on top, like the spinner is teetering while it turns. Quicker and more nervous than a wide orbit.

name: orbit-loop
concept: A wide circular path traced while the element also rotates in place, like a small moon orbiting a point while turning on its own axis. The largest of the orbit variants.

name: spin-jitter-orbit
concept: A fast rotation with small, irregular position jitters instead of a smooth circular drift. Reads as nervous, urgent activity rather than calm orbiting.

name: orbit-sway
concept: A slow, gentle circular drift with a full rotation, tracing a calm and simple loop. The most relaxed of the orbit variants.

name: spin-grow
concept: A rotation that grows steadily larger across the turn, then resets to its starting size at the next loop. Suggests a process building toward something.

name: spin-expand-reset
concept: A rotation that grows and fades slightly toward the end of its turn before snapping back to full size and opacity. Reads as a stronger build-up than spin-grow.

name: spin-balloon
concept: A rotation where the element inflates past its target size before settling, like a balloon overfilled then eased back. Bouncier than a plain growth spin.

name: spin-zoom-loop
concept: A quick rotation with a strong, steady scale increase across the turn, then a sharp snap back to start. Feels fast and forward-driving, like zooming ahead.

name: spin-amplify
concept: A smoothly rotating element that grows in four distinct size steps, one per quarter-turn, then resets. The contrast between smooth turning and stepped growth reads as building intensity.

name: gyrate
concept: A rotation layered with a gentle side-to-side skew, giving the turn a slightly warped, two-axis feel without any 3D. A livelier alternative to a flat spin.

name: gyrate-tilt
concept: A rotation with a stronger vertical skew than the base gyrate, giving each turn a pronounced tilting, top-heavy feel. Reads as a heavier, more exaggerated wobble.

name: gyrate-twist
concept: A rotation where the skew shifts from one axis in the first half of the turn to the other axis in the second half, giving a twisting, figure-like motion.

name: gyrate-flutter
concept: A fast rotation with rapid, small skew oscillations layered throughout, like a fluttering flag caught in the turn. Busier and quicker than the base gyrate.

name: gyrate-lean
concept: A rotation with an uneven skew, leaning further one way than it corrects on the other. Gives the turn a lopsided, off-balance character.

name: gyrate-shear
concept: A slow rotation with one strong vertical shear peak at the midpoint, like the shape briefly shearing sideways mid-turn. Heavier and simpler than the twist variant.

name: spin-urgent
concept: A very fast rotation with a tiny scale kick each turn, reading as urgent, high-priority activity. Faster than a standard spin, with a hint of pressure.

name: spin-blitz
concept: A very fast rotation with a brief opacity flicker each turn, like a quick flash of activity. Reads as an intense, momentary burst of work.

name: spin-frenzy
concept: A very fast, unevenly paced rotation that speeds and slows erratically within the turn. Reads as frantic, high-intensity activity rather than steady work.

name: spin-dash
concept: A very fast rotation with a brief horizontal squish each turn, suggesting a streak or motion blur. Feels like a quick dash rather than a plain fast spin.

name: spin-stately
concept: A very slow rotation with a smooth ease-in-out through each turn, reading as calm and dignified. Suits a background process with no urgency.

name: spin-regal
concept: An extremely slow, constant-speed rotation with a faint scale breath, reading as calm and composed. The slowest and evenest of the family.

name: spin-ponder
concept: A slow rotation that pauses at each quarter-turn as if considering before continuing, like someone pondering a decision. Deliberate and unhurried.

name: spin-drift-slow
concept: A slow rotation with a very small, gentle circular drift, like a leaf turning slowly on still water. Meditative and understated.

name: spin-pendulum
concept: The element swings forward then reverses back to its start, like a pendulum, instead of completing a full rotation. Loops smoothly as a back-and-forth motion.

name: spin-seesaw
concept: The element tips one way, then the other, then levels out, like a seesaw rocking through its middle. A sharper back-and-forth than the pendulum swing.

name: spin-tug
concept: The rotation moves forward, briefly pulls back as if tugged, then continues on to complete the turn. A single reversal inside an otherwise forward spin.

name: spin-waver
concept: The rotation edges forward with several small backward wavers along the way, like a hand that keeps hesitating before completing its turn. Net progress with visible hesitation.

name: orbit-tick
concept: A stepped rotation, paused at four points like a compass, that also shifts position slightly at each stop. Like a turret ticking between fixed headings.

name: spin-windup-fast
concept: A very short, sharply accelerating rotation that ends with a small scale kick, like a spring released under urgency. Combines the wind-up feel with high speed.

name: gyrate-pulse
concept: A rotation with a side-to-side skew that peaks alongside a small scale pulse, combining the warped feel of gyrate with a soft breathing beat.
